title: 2018 AMC 12B Problem 24
statement: Let \(\lfloor x\rfloor\) denote the greatest integer less than or equal to \(x.\) How many real numbers \(x\) satisfy the equation \(x^2+10{,}000\lfloor x\rfloor=10{,}000x?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(\{x\}=x-\lfloor x\rfloor.\) The equation becomes \(x^2=10{,}000\{x\},\) so \(\tfrac{x^2}{10{,}000}=\{x\}.\) Since \(0\le\{x\}\lt1,\) we need \(0\le x^2\lt10{,}000,\) i.e. \(-100\lt x\lt100.\)

On each interval \([k,k+1),\) write \(x=k+t\) with \(0\le t\lt1.\) The equation becomes \((k+t)^2-10{,}000t=0.\) For \(-100\le k\le98,\) the left side is strictly decreasing; at \(t=0\) it is \(k^2\ge0,\) while as \(t\) approaches \(1\) it approaches \((k+1)^2-10{,}000\lt0.\) Thus each of these intervals contains exactly one solution. There are \(98-(-100)+1=199\) such intervals.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Then \(0\le\dfrac{x^2}{10{,}000}\lt1,\) so \(-100\lt x\lt100;\) count one solution per unit interval
